svg.title: The simulated single-sided proton CT scanner, seen from above, to scale
svg.text: The simulated scanner, seen from above, to scale
Beam nozzle: 330 MeV pencil beams, spot after spot,
7 mm apart (x ±196 mm, z ±56 mm), σ 3.7 mm;
the beam log gives each proton’s spot
from a patient CT, turned 1° between views:
360 views. Its middle slice, with the
kidneys and the liver; every voxel’s RSP is known
ALPIDE pixel chips and 3.5 mm of
proton stops gives its range, so its WEPL
No detector before the patient: the scanner knows a proton’s entry only from its spot.
